articleBody:
Before starting demolition on a guest bathroom, reviewing your materials, plans, and compliance details protects you from costly project halts. Use this practical preparation list before work begins.

- [ ] Written scope of work — Confirms exactly which fixtures, tile areas, and electrical connections are scheduled for replacement.
- [ ] Local permit requirements verified — Identifies whether moving plumbing, altering wiring, or replacing the shower pan requires municipal trade permits.
- [ ] Existing subfloor moisture inspection — Checks under existing vinyl or tile around the toilet and tub to catch concealed subfloor rot early.
- [ ] 2-inch shower drain path confirmed — Ensures your floor framing accommodates the larger drain pipe required if converting from a bathtub to a walk-in shower.
- [ ] Outdoor ventilation duct route mapped — Verifies that the bathroom exhaust fan vents directly outdoors rather than discharging humid air into your attic.
- [ ] Dedicated 20-amp GFCI circuit confirmed — Ensures your electrical setup meets current bathroom receptacle safety standards.
- [ ] Finished fixture spec sheets compiled — Provides plumbing and electrical trades with exact rough-in dimensions for the sink, vanity, and shower valve.
- [ ] Contingency line item for hidden damage — Reserves 10 to 15 percent of your budget for unforeseen pipe corrosion or structural framing repairs behind older walls.

### How to use this checklist
Review these items with your general contractor during the planning stage before ordering specialty finishes or swinging hammers.
